_comment: TEMPORAL-EXTRAPOLATION EXPERIMENT, run 1985. Withholds 1966-1985 (20 years) from the DESK objective entirely, so those years test extrapolation BACKWARD beyond the training data -- the direction the 1900 use case needs. Run the three overlays (1975/1985/1995) to get skill against extrapolation distance. desk.trend.seed is NOT overridden anywhere: the spatial split must stay identical across the three or the decay curve is confounded by a moving holdout. Direction anchors are PINNED and identical across the three overlays. direction_anchor_year=1996 is the trained-era CONTROL: the deepest year every run trained on, so the interval is a constant 1996->2025 and the IDW bar exists in all three. It isolates 'did losing the deep past hurt modern-era skill' from extrapolation -- and measures no extrapolation itself, since both ends lie in trained years. direction_withheld_anchor_year=1975 is the MEASUREMENT: withheld in all three, 1,645 routes, a constant 1975->2025 interval whose extrapolation DISTANCE varies by design (1 yr past the training edge in the 1975 run, 11 in 1985, 21 in 1995 -- that variation IS the independent variable). It is deliberately not 1966: BBS's launch year, ~400 routes / ~351 cells, which after the anchor intersection and the val split is the ~36-val-cell case DEFAULT_EPOCHS was written to avoid. common_holdout_years=1966-1975 is the window withheld in EVERY run; restricting the reported buckets to it is what makes the three runs comparable, because each run's own full block is dominated by its shallow, cheap end (BBS coverage grows ~7x from 1966 to 1995, and a 10.8 yr EMA half-life makes a 1-2 year reach close to interpolation). Usage: ESK_DESK_CONFIG=config/overlays/desk_tempho_1985.json STAGES=desk bash scripts/tacc/submit_encoder.sh
